pillars.label: GDPR Art. 33
pillars.title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
pillars.fact: Report a personal data breach to the supervisory authority within 72 hours, where feasible — late ones need reasons.

pillars.label: GDPR Art. 83
pillars.title: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
pillars.fact: Fines of up to €20 million or 4% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.

pillars.label: GDPR Art. 7
pillars.title: Conditions for consent
pillars.fact: Withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it.
pillars.evidence: withdraw his or her consent at any time

pillars.label: GDPR Art. 17
pillars.title: Right to erasure (‘right to be forgotten’)
pillars.fact: The right to erasure: personal data must go without undue delay. Your startup may follow.

pillars.label: GDPR Art. 37
pillars.title: Designation of the data protection officer
pillars.fact: A data protection officer is mandatory when your core activity is regular and systematic monitoring of people on a large scale.

pillars.label: GDPR Art. 35
pillars.title: Data protection impact assessment
pillars.fact: High-risk processing needs a data protection impact assessment before it starts.

pillars.label: GDPR Art. 25
pillars.title: Data protection by design and by default
pillars.fact: Data protection by design and by default — from the moment you decide how to process.

pillars.label: AI Act Art. 5
pillars.title: Prohibited AI practices
pillars.fact: Emotion recognition in the workplace and in education is prohibited, save for medical or safety reasons.

pillars.label: AI Act Art. 99
pillars.title: Penalties
pillars.fact: Breaching the Art. 5 prohibitions: up to €35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover. For start-ups, mercifully, whichever is lower.

pillars.label: AI Act Art. 50
pillars.title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
pillars.fact: Deep fakes must be disclosed as artificially generated or manipulated.

pillars.label: AI Act Art. 4
pillars.title: AI literacy
pillars.fact: Providers and deployers must ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff.

pillars.label: AI Act Art. 113
pillars.title: Entry into force and application
pillars.fact: The prohibitions applied from 2 February 2025; most of the rest from 2 August 2026.

pillars.label: AI Act Art. 11
pillars.title: Technical documentation
pillars.fact: Technical documentation for a high-risk AI system is drawn up before it is placed on the market — Annex IV lists what goes in.

pillars.label: AI Act Art. 14
pillars.title: Human oversight
pillars.fact: High-risk AI systems must be designed so natural persons can effectively oversee them.

pillars.label: NIS2 Art. 23
pillars.title: Reporting obligations
pillars.fact: Significant incidents: early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, final report within one month.

pillars.label: NIS2 Art. 34
pillars.title: General conditions for imposing administrative fines on essential and important entities
pillars.fact: Essential entities: fines of a maximum of at least €10 million or 2% of worldwide annual turnover.

pillars.label: NIS2 Art. 20
pillars.title: Governance
pillars.fact: Management bodies approve the cybersecurity measures, can be held liable, and must follow training.

pillars.label: NIS2 Art. 21
pillars.title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures
pillars.fact: Cybersecurity risk-management measures include supply chain security and multi-factor authentication.

pillars.label: DORA Art. 19
pillars.title: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents and voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
pillars.fact: Financial entities must report major ICT-related incidents to their competent authority.

pillars.label: DORA Art. 26
pillars.title: Advanced testing of ICT tools, systems and processes based on TLPT
pillars.fact: Threat-led penetration testing, on live production systems, at least every 3 years.

pillars.label: DORA Art. 28
pillars.title: General principles
pillars.fact: Financial entities keep a register of information on every contract with an ICT third-party provider.

pillars.label: DORA Art. 64
pillars.title: Entry into force and application
pillars.fact: Applies from 17 January 2025. Your runway did not.

pillars.label: DSA Art. 52
pillars.title: Penalties
pillars.fact: Breaking the DSA costs up to 6% of annual worldwide turnover; misleading the regulator, another 1%.

pillars.label: DSA Art. 16
pillars.title: Notice and action mechanisms
pillars.fact: Hosting services must let anyone flag illegal content, electronically and user-friendly. Your rocket has been flagged.

pillars.label: DSA Art. 34
pillars.title: Risk assessment
pillars.fact: Very large platforms must assess their systemic risks at least once every year, and before launching risky features.
pillars.evidence: at least once every year thereafter

pillars.label: DMA Art. 30
pillars.title: Fines
pillars.fact: Gatekeepers face fines of up to 10% of worldwide turnover, 20% for a repeat. Congratulations on being big enough.

pillars.label: DMA Art. 3
pillars.title: Designation of gatekeepers
pillars.fact: Presumed gatekeeper from €7.5 billion annual EU turnover or €75 billion market cap. Your seed round is not concerned.

pillars.label: CRA Art. 64
pillars.title: Penalties
pillars.fact: Ignoring the essential cybersecurity requirements: up to €15 million or 2.5% of worldwide turnover.

pillars.label: CRA Art. 14
pillars.title: Reporting obligations of manufacturers
pillars.fact: Actively exploited vulnerability? Early warning to the CSIRT and ENISA within 24 hours.
pillars.evidence: within 24 hours of the manufacturer becoming aware

pillars.label: Data Act Art. 3
pillars.title: Obligation to make product data and related service data accessible to the user
pillars.fact: Connected products must be designed so users can access their own data, by default. Including the toaster.

pillars.label: Data Act Art. 29
pillars.title: Gradual withdrawal of switching charges
pillars.fact: From 12 January 2027, cloud providers may not charge you for switching away. Leaving is free; staying is not.
pillars.evidence: From 12 January 2027, providers of data processing services shall not impose any switching charges

pillars.label: eIDAS 2 Art. 5a
pillars.title: European Digital Identity Wallets
pillars.fact: Each Member State must provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months of the implementing acts.
pillars.evidence: at least one European Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months

pillars.label: eIDAS 2 Art. 16
pillars.title: Penalties
pillars.fact: Trust service providers face fines of at least €5 million or 1% of worldwide turnover.
pillars.evidence: EUR 5 000 000 or 1 % of the total worldwide annual turnover

pillars.label: CSRD Art. 19a
pillars.title: Sustainability reporting
pillars.fact: Report your impacts on sustainability and how sustainability affects you. Both directions, audited.

pillars.label: CSRD Art. 29b
pillars.title: Sustainability reporting standards
pillars.fact: The sustainability reporting standards arrive by delegated act. Of course they do.
pillars.evidence: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts

pillars.label: ePrivacy Art. 5
pillars.title: Confidentiality of the communications
pillars.fact: Storing or reading information on a user's device (yes, cookies) is only allowed if they agree. Hence the banner.
pillars.evidence: the storing of information, or the gaining of access to information already stored

pillars.label: ePrivacy Art. 13
pillars.title: Unsolicited communications
pillars.fact: Direct-marketing e-mail needs prior consent; existing customers get the soft opt-in.
pillars.evidence: who have given their prior consent

sandbox.label: AI Act Art. 57
sandbox.title: AI regulatory sandboxes
sandbox.fact: Every Member State must have at least one AI regulatory sandbox operational by 2 August 2026. The sand is not yet harmonised.

delegated.label: AI Act Art. 7
delegated.title: Amendments to Annex III
delegated.fact: The Commission is empowered to amend Annex III by delegated act. The pillars have been relocated.
